items.readable_text:
Content:
The circumference of a circle is the length of the path that goes around the circle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f1e77c0cd2f2322435cd574b1b205c04]

Content:
The circumference is usually denoted by the letter [MATH: C.]

Content:
One important fact about the circumference is that, for any circle, no matter how small or large it is, the ratio of circumference [MATH: C] to diameter [MATH: d] is a fixed number! Specifically,
[MATH: \dfrac{C}{d} = {\color{blue}\boldsymbol{\pi}} \approx 3.141\,592\,654...]

Content:
This important irrational number is called pi (pronounced "pie") and we use the Greek letter [MATH: \pi] to express it. So, we can calculate the circumference by using the following formula:

Content:
[MATH: C = πd.]

Content:
Here, our circle has diameter [MATH: 4\,\textrm{cm},] so its circumference is
[MATH: C = \pi \cdot 4 = 4\pi \approx 12.566\,\mathrm{cm},]
rounded to three decimal digits.

Content:
Since the diameter is twice as long as the radius ([MATH: d=2r]), we can also write the formula for the circumference as
[MATH: C = \pi d = 2\pi r.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We use the formula [MATH: C=\pi d] and get

[MATH: C|= πd; = π ⋅ 10; = 10π.]

This is the exact answer. If we want an approximate answer, say rounded to three decimal places, we can use the approximation [MATH: \pi\approx 3.14\,159,] and we get

[MATH: C|= 10 ⋅ π; ≈ 10 ⋅ 3.14159; ≈ 31.416.]
